grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain home staple: lentils, spinach, eggs, flour, feta, yoghurt, radishes and spring onions.

supermarket.reason: Everything is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a saucepan, sieve and frying pan are needed, and shallow-frying spoonfuls is beginner technique.

works.reason: 150g red lentils in 400ml water cooks soft without much excess, and the eggs and flour bind it well enough to fry four portions of fritters.

honest_times.reason: Slicing spring onions and radishes, crumbling feta and zesting fit in 15 minutes, and a 10-minute simmer plus two 6-minute frying batches matches the 25 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the lemon as both zest and juice, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Late April spinach is wilted into the body of the fritters, so it is the point of the dish, and a light fritter lunch with radishes suits spring.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils, eggs, feta and spinach with yoghurt and radishes make a filling, balanced lunch a family would eat again.
